recipes.title: Beef bulgogi
recipes.blurb: Sweet-savory marinated ribeye, seared hot and fast

steps.text: Stir the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, grated pear and pepper in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Add the beef, onion and half the green onions. Toss well to coat.
Cover and marinate in the fridge, at least 30 minutes and up to 8 hours.
Heat a large skillet or cast iron pan over high heat with the oil.
Cook the beef in two batches, 2 to 3 minutes each, until browned at the edges. Do not crowd the pan.
Top with sesame seeds and remaining green onions. Serve over rice.

recipes.title: LA galbi (grilled short ribs)
recipes.blurb: Flanken-cut short ribs with a sweet soy-pear marinade

ingredients.item: flanken-cut beef short ribs (0.5 inch thick)

steps.text: Whisk soy sauce, sugar, water, sesame oil, pear, garlic, ginger, green onions and pepper until the sugar dissolves.
Place the ribs in a large zip bag or dish and pour the marinade over. Turn to coat.
Marinate in the fridge, at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a grill or grill pan to high. Lift ribs out and let extra marinade drip off.
Grill 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Rest the ribs, then snip between the bones with scissors. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Spicy pork bulgogi
recipes.blurb: Gochujang-marinated pork shoulder with a sticky char

steps.text: Mix gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic and ginger into a paste.
Toss the pork with the paste, onion and green onions until evenly coated.
Marinate in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the pork in batches, 4 to 5 minutes, until browned and cooked through to 145°F.
Serve with lettuce leaves and rice for wrapping.

recipes.title: Samgyeopsal lettuce wraps
recipes.blurb: Crispy pork belly with ssamjang in lettuce leaves

ingredients.item: sliced pork belly (0.25 inch thick, skinless)

steps.text: Mix doenjang, gochujang, sesame oil, minced garlic and green onions in a small bowl. This is the ssamjang.
Pat the pork belly dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat a large skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat. Add the pork in one layer, working in batches.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and crisp at the edges.
Add the sliced garlic to the pan during the last 2 minutes to soften and brown.
Cut the pork into bite-size pieces. Wrap in lettuce with rice, garlic and a dab of ssamjang.

recipes.title: Soy-garlic chicken bulgogi
recipes.blurb: Mild, sweet and fast. A big hit with kids

steps.text: Mix soy sauce, sugar, honey, sesame oil, garlic and ginger in a bowl. Add the chicken and toss to coat.
Marinate for 15 minutes while you slice the vegetables.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook 3 minutes.
Push the vegetables aside, add the chicken and cook 6 to 7 minutes until browned and cooked to 165°F.
Toss everything together, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve over rice.

recipes.title: Korean chicken skewers (dak kkochi)
recipes.blurb: Glazed gochujang-soy chicken on sticks, grilled or broiled

steps.text: Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil and garlic. Save a few tablespoons in a small bowl for glazing.
Toss the chicken in the remaining sauce and thread onto skewers, alternating with green onion.
Let the skewers sit in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and brush with oil.
Grill 12 to 14 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Brush with the saved sauce in the last 2 minutes. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Dak galbi (spicy stir-fried chicken)
recipes.blurb: Chicken, cabbage and rice cakes in a fiery gochujang sauce

steps.text: Mix gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and garlic. Toss with the chicken.
Marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the sweet potato and rice cakes and cook 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, onion and cabbage. Stir often and cook 12 to 15 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F and the sweet potato is soft.
Fold in the perilla leaves for the last minute. Serve from the pan with rice.

recipes.title: Spicy stir-fried squid
recipes.blurb: Tender squid and vegetables in a hot, glossy sauce

steps.text: Mix gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and garlic in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Cook the onion, carrot and pepper 2 minutes.
Add the squid and sauce. Stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes only, until the squid is opaque and curled.
Add the green onions and toss 30 seconds. Serve right away with rice. Overcooked squid turns rubbery.

recipes.title: Bibimbap
recipes.blurb: Rice topped with seasoned vegetables, beef and a fried egg

steps.text: Season the beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil and half the garlic. Cook in a skillet to 160°F, then set aside.
Boil the sprouts in water for 5 minutes, drain, and toss with 1 tsp sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Blanch the spinach 30 seconds, squeeze dry, and toss with the remaining garlic, 1 tsp sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Saute the zucchini and carrot separately in the vegetable oil, 2 to 3 minutes each, with a pinch of salt.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in a little oil.
Divide rice among bowls. Arrange the toppings, add an egg and 1 tbsp gochujang each. Drizzle with sesame oil and mix well to eat.

recipes.title: Bulgogi rice bowl
recipes.blurb: Quick marinated beef over rice with cucumber and carrot

steps.text: Toss the beef with soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil and garlic. Let it sit 10 minutes.
Let the beef marinate while the rice warms.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Cook the beef in two batches, 2 minutes each, until browned.
Spoon rice into bowls. Top with beef, cucumber, carrot, green onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Kimchi fried rice
recipes.blurb: Day-old rice, tangy kimchi and a runny fried egg

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Cook the bacon or spam until browned, about 4 minutes.
Add the kimchi and juice. Cook 3 minutes until it softens and smells tangy.
Stir in the gochujang and soy sauce, then add the rice, breaking up clumps.
Stir-fry 4 minutes until hot and lightly crisp. Mix in the sesame oil and green onions.
In a second pan, fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set and the yolks runny.
Top each bowl of rice with an egg, sesame seeds and seaweed.

recipes.title: Kimbap (Korean seaweed rice rolls)
recipes.blurb: Rolls of rice, egg, carrot, spinach and beef, sliced in rounds

steps.text: Season the warm rice with 1 tbsp sesame oil, half the salt and the sesame seeds. Let cool a few minutes.
Cook the beaten eggs as a thin omelet in the vegetable oil, then slice into strips.
Saute the carrot 2 minutes with a pinch of salt. Blanch the spinach 30 seconds, squeeze dry and toss with a little sesame oil and salt.
Lay a seaweed sheet shiny-side down. Spread a thin layer of rice, leaving 1 inch bare at the top edge.
Arrange egg, carrot, cucumber, spinach, radish and beef in a line along the bottom third. Roll tightly and seal with a dab of water.
Brush the roll with sesame oil and slice into 1-inch rounds with a sharp, wet knife.

recipes.title: Spicy pork rice bowl (jeyuk deopbap)
recipes.blurb: Gochujang pork stir-fry over rice with a fried egg

steps.text: Mix gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and garlic. Toss with the pork.
Marinate at least 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion 2 minutes.
Add the pork and cook 6 to 8 minutes until browned and cooked to 145°F. Stir in the green onions.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil.
Serve the pork over rice, topped with an egg.

recipes.title: Tuna mayo rice bowl
recipes.blurb: Pantry tuna, mayo and soy over rice. Ready in 10 minutes

ingredients.item: chunk light tuna in water (5 oz)

steps.text: Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, 1 tsp soy sauce, sugar and green onions in a bowl.
Toss the warm rice with the sesame oil and remaining soy sauce.
Divide the rice into bowls and top with the tuna mixture and cucumber.
Sprinkle with seaweed and sesame seeds. Serve right away.

recipes.title: Butter soy egg rice (gyeran bap)
recipes.blurb: Fried eggs, butter and soy over hot rice. Comfort in 5 minutes

steps.text: Put the hot rice into two bowls and add 1 tbsp butter to each. Let it melt.
Fry the eggs in a nonstick skillet over medium heat, 2 to 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
Top each bowl with two eggs.
Drizzle with soy sauce and sesame oil. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and seaweed, then stir everything together to eat.

recipes.title: Mushroom rice bowl (beoseot deopbap)
recipes.blurb: Garlicky soy-glazed mushrooms over rice, fully vegan

steps.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms in a single layer. Cook 6 to 8 minutes without stirring too much, until browned.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Stir in the soy sauce and maple syrup and cook 1 minute until glossy. Turn off the heat and add the sesame oil.
Serve over rice with the carrot, green onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Japchae (glass noodle stir-fry)
recipes.blurb: Chewy sweet potato noodles with beef and colorful vegetables

steps.text: Toss the beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil, half the garlic and pepper.
Boil the noodles until soft and chewy, then drain, rinse and cut a few times with scissors.
Blanch the spinach 30 seconds, squeeze dry and toss with a little soy sauce and sesame oil.
Stir-fry the onion, carrot, mushrooms and pepper in 2 tbsp vegetable oil with a pinch of salt, one at a time, 2 minutes each.
Cook the beef in the remaining oil until browned, about 3 minutes, to 160°F.
Toss the noodles in the pan with the remaining soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and garlic for 2 minutes.
Mix in the vegetables, beef and spinach. Top with sesame seeds and serve warm or room temperature.

recipes.title: Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles)
recipes.blurb: Thick noodles in a savory-sweet black bean sauce with pork

ingredients.item: fresh or dried udon or jajangmyeon noodles

steps.text: Fry the chunjang in the oil in a skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, to remove bitterness. Scoop it out.
In the same pan, cook the pork 4 minutes until browned and cooked to 160°F.
Add the onion, zucchini and potato. Stir-fry 3 minutes.
Return the black bean paste, add sugar, soy sauce and 1.5 cups water. Simmer until the potato is tender.
Simmer the sauce.
Stir the cornstarch with 2 tbsp water and add it. Cook 1 minute until glossy.
Boil the noodles per the package, drain, and top with the sauce and cucumber.

recipes.title: Bibim guksu (spicy chilled noodles)
recipes.blurb: Tangy, sweet and spicy somen noodles with cucumber and egg

steps.text: Whisk gochujang, gochugaru, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil and garlic into a sauce.
Boil the noodles until tender.
Drain and rinse the noodles under cold water, rubbing gently, until cold. Drain well.
Toss the noodles with the sauce until coated.
Top with cucumber, kimchi, egg halves and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Chicken kalguksu (noodle soup)
recipes.blurb: Hand-cut-style noodles in a clean chicken broth

steps.text: Put the chicken, water, onion, garlic and ginger in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then lower to a simmer.
Simmer until the chicken is 165°F.
Lift out the chicken and shred it. Strain the broth and return it to the pot, discarding the solids.
Season the broth with soy sauce and salt. Bring to a boil and add the carrot and noodles.
Cook the noodles until tender, adding the zucchini for the last minute.
Slowly drizzle in the egg while stirring. Serve topped with chicken and green onions.

recipes.title: Janchi guksu (banquet noodles)
recipes.blurb: Light anchovy broth with thin noodles, zucchini and egg ribbons

ingredients.note: beaten, cooked as a thin omelet and sliced

steps.text: Bring water, anchovies and kelp to a boil. Remove the kelp after 5 minutes.
Simmer the broth 15 minutes, then strain and return to the pot.
Season the broth with soy sauce and salt. Keep it warm.
Saute the zucchini and carrot separately in a little oil for 2 minutes each.
Boil the noodles in a separate pot, then rinse in cold water and drain.
Place noodles in bowls and ladle hot broth over. Top with vegetables, egg strips, green onions, sesame seeds and a drizzle of sesame oil.

recipes.title: Kongguksu (cold soy milk noodles)
recipes.blurb: Silky, nutty soybean broth over chilled noodles. A summer classic

ingredients.item: raw peanuts or toasted pine nuts

steps.text: Blend the soy milk, peanuts, sesame seeds and salt until very smooth.
Chill the broth in the freezer 15 minutes while you cook the noodles.
Boil the somen until tender.
Drain and rinse the noodles in cold water, then drain very well.
Divide noodles among bowls and pour the cold broth over. Add a few ice cubes if you like.
Top with cucumber and tomato. Add salt to taste at the table.

recipes.title: Kimchi ramyeon with egg
recipes.blurb: Instant noodles dressed up with kimchi, tofu and green onion

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil in a medium pot. Add the kimchi, kimchi juice, tofu and soup base from the packets.
Simmer the kimchi 3 minutes.
Add the noodles. Use chopsticks to loosen them.
Cook the noodles until tender.
Crack in the eggs during the last minute and let them set to your liking.
Finish with green onions and sesame oil. Eat right away.

recipes.title: Rabokki (ramyeon with spicy rice cakes)
recipes.blurb: Chewy rice cakes and noodles in a bubbly red sauce

ingredients.item: Korean instant ramyeon (3 oz), noodles only

steps.text: Soak the rice cakes in warm water 10 minutes if hard or refrigerated.
Stir the water, gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce and sugar together in a wide pan and bring to a boil.
Add the rice cakes, fish cakes and eggs.
Simmer until the rice cakes are soft and the sauce thickens, stirring often.
Add the ramyeon noodles and green onions.
Cook until the noodles are tender and the sauce coats everything.

recipes.title: Kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew)
recipes.blurb: Sour, spicy stew with pork belly and tofu. The everyday favorite

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Cook the pork until it just turns pale, about 3 minutes.
Add the kimchi, garlic and gochugaru and stir 3 minutes.
Add the kimchi juice, gochujang and water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce to a simmer, cover partly and cook until the kimchi is soft and the pork is 145°F or higher.
Add the tofu and onion and simmer 5 more minutes.
Finish with green onions and sesame oil. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew)
recipes.blurb: Earthy, savory stew with tofu, zucchini and potato

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil in a pot. Whisk in the doenjang and gochugaru until dissolved.
Add the potato and onion and simmer until the potato is nearly tender.
Simmer the potato and onion.
Add the zucchini, mushrooms and garlic. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add the tofu and chili and simmer 3 more minutes.
Top with green onions and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew)
recipes.blurb: Bubbling, spicy silken tofu stew with an egg cracked in

steps.text: Heat the oil and sesame oil in a small pot over medium heat. Cook the meat and garlic 3 minutes.
Stir in the gochugaru for 30 seconds, being careful not to burn it.
Add the water and soy sauce and bring to a boil.
Spoon in the tofu in large chunks. Add the seafood if using.
Simmer until the stew bubbles hard and the meat is cooked through.
Crack in the egg and add the green onions. Cover for 1 minute. Season with salt and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Budae jjigae (army stew)
recipes.blurb: Spam, sausage, kimchi, noodles and cheese in a spicy broth

steps.text: Whisk the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic with the water in a wide pot.
Arrange the kimchi, spam, sausages, tofu and beans in sections around the pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer.
Add the ramyeon noodles and the soup base if you like it extra salty.
Cook until the noodles are tender.
Lay on the cheese slices and green onions. Serve right away from the pot.

recipes.title: Yukgaejang (spicy beef and vegetable soup)
recipes.blurb: Shredded beef, scallions and bracken in a fiery red broth

steps.text: Simmer the beef, water and onion in a large pot, skimming off foam.
Cook the beef until very tender.
Lift out the beef. Shred it into strands and discard the onion.
Mix the beef with garlic, gochugaru, soy sauce and sesame oil.
Return it to the broth with the green onions, sprouts and fernbrake.
Simmer the soup.
Stir in the beaten egg in a thin stream. Season with salt and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Tteokguk (rice cake soup)
recipes.blurb: Clear beef broth with chewy rice cake coins, a New Year tradition

steps.text: Soak the rice cakes in cold water 20 minutes, then drain.
Cook the beef in 1 tbsp sesame oil in a pot for 2 minutes. Add half the garlic and 1 tbsp soy sauce.
Add the water, bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes. Skim the foam.
Simmer the broth.
Add the rice cakes, remaining soy sauce, garlic and salt.
Cook until the rice cakes float and are soft.
Beat and scramble the eggs into a thin sheet, slice into ribbons. Top bowls with egg, green onions, seaweed and pepper.

recipes.title: Miyeok guk (seaweed soup)
recipes.blurb: Mild, comforting seaweed and beef soup, the classic birthday soup

steps.text: Soak the seaweed in cold water until fully expanded.
Drain, rinse and squeeze out the water. Cut into 2-inch pieces.
Heat the sesame oil in a pot. Cook the beef 3 minutes, then add the seaweed, garlic and soy sauce and stir 3 minutes.
Add the water and bring to a boil.
Simmer until the seaweed is silky and the beef tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes)
recipes.blurb: Chewy rice cakes and fish cakes in a sweet, spicy gochujang sauce

steps.text: If the rice cakes are hard, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes and drain.
Whisk the water, gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce and sugar in a wide pan and bring to a boil.
Add the rice cakes and fish cakes.
Simmer, stirring often, until the rice cakes are soft and the sauce is thick and glossy.
Add the eggs and green onions and cook 2 minutes.
Top with sesame seeds and serve hot.

recipes.title: Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup)
recipes.blurb: Whole small chicken stuffed with rice, simmered until falling-apart tender

steps.text: Drain the rice. Fill each hen cavity with rice, 3 garlic cloves and 2 jujubes.
Tie the legs together with kitchen twine and cross them to hold the stuffing in.
Place the hens in a pot with the ginger, ginseng if using, and the water.
Bring to a boil, cover, then simmer on low until the rice is cooked and the chicken is 165°F.
Skim off foam. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve each hen in a bowl with broth, green onions and a small dish of salt and pepper.

recipes.title: Yangnyeom chicken (sweet-spicy fried chicken)
recipes.blurb: Double-fried crunchy chicken tossed in a sticky gochujang glaze

steps.text: Pat the chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper. Mix cornstarch, flour, egg and water into a thin batter and coat the chicken.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 340°F.
Fry the chicken in batches until light golden. Rest on a rack.
Raise the oil to 375°F.
Fry again until deep golden and very crisp. Chicken must reach 165°F.
Simmer gochujang, ketchup, honey, soy sauce and garlic in a pan 2 minutes until sticky.
Toss the chicken in the sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Soy-garlic chicken wings
recipes.blurb: Crisp air-fried wings in a sweet soy and garlic glaze

steps.text: Pat the wings dry. Toss with baking powder and salt.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F. Arrange the wings in a single layer, in batches.
Air fry, flipping halfway, until crisp and 165°F inside.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Cook the garlic 30 seconds, then add soy sauce, honey and vinegar.
Simmer the glaze until syrupy.
Toss the wings in the glaze. Top with sesame seeds and green onions.

recipes.title: Dakgangjeong (crunchy sweet chicken bites)
recipes.blurb: Crispy chicken pieces in a sticky sweet soy glaze

steps.text: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Toss in starch until coated.
Heat 1.5 inches of oil in a pot to 350°F.
Fry the chicken in batches until golden and 165°F inside.
Cook the soy sauce, sugar, syrup, water and garlic in a pan over medium heat.
Simmer the sauce until it thickens and bubbles.
Toss the hot chicken in the sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Kimchijeon (kimchi pancake)
recipes.blurb: Crispy-edged savory pancake with sour kimchi

steps.text: Whisk flour, cornstarch, water, egg, kimchi juice and sugar until just smooth.
Fold in the kimchi and green onions.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Spread half the batter thin.
Cook until the underside is deeply golden and crisp.
Flip, press down, and cook the other side 3 more minutes. Repeat with the rest.
Cut into squares. Mix soy sauce and vinegar for dipping.

recipes.title: Pajeon (green onion pancake)
recipes.blurb: Chewy-crisp pancake loaded with green onions

steps.text: Whisk flour, cornstarch, water, egg and salt into a smooth batter, thin like crepe batter.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Lay half the green onions in the pan.
Pour half the batter over the onions to cover.
Cook until the bottom is golden and crisp.
Flip and cook 3 more minutes, pressing with a spatula. Repeat with the rest.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar and gochugaru as a dip. Cut the pancakes into squares.

recipes.title: Haemul pajeon (seafood scallion pancake)
recipes.blurb: Shrimp and squid in a crisp scallion pancake

steps.text: Whisk flour, cornstarch, water, egg and salt into a thin batter. Stir in the shrimp and squid.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Lay half the green onions in the pan.
Pour on half the batter and seafood, spreading to cover.
Cook until the bottom is crisp and golden.
Flip and cook 3 more minutes until the seafood is opaque. Repeat with the rest.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar and gochugaru. Serve with the pancake cut in squares.

recipes.title: Gamjajeon (potato pancakes)
recipes.blurb: Grated potato pancakes, crisp outside and chewy inside

steps.text: Grate the potatoes on the small holes of a box grater into a bowl. Let them sit 5 minutes.
Pour off the thin liquid on top but keep the white starch at the bottom. Mix the starch back into the potato.
Stir in the onion, salt and green onions.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Spoon in the batter and press into thin pancakes.
Cook until deep golden and crisp.
Flip, add a little oil, and cook 3 minutes more. Serve with soy-vinegar dip.

recipes.title: Gun-mandu (pan-fried dumplings)
recipes.blurb: Crisp-bottomed pork and vegetable dumplings

ingredients.note: finely chopped, salted and squeezed dry

steps.text: Mix the pork, cabbage, tofu, green onions, garlic, 1 tbsp soy sauce and sesame oil until well combined.
Place 1 tbsp filling in the center of each wrapper. Wet the edge, fold in half and pinch tight.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add dumplings flat-side down.
Cook until the bottoms are golden.
Add the water, cover quickly and steam until the water is gone.
Steam the dumplings.
Uncover and crisp 1 minute more. Pork must reach 160°F. Serve with soy sauce and vinegar to dip.

recipes.title: Kongnamul muchim (seasoned soybean sprouts)
recipes.blurb: Crunchy, nutty sprouts with garlic and sesame

steps.text: Rinse the sprouts and discard any loose bean hulls.
Put the sprouts and water in a pot, cover and bring to a boil.
Steam covered without lifting the lid, then drain and cool.
Toss the warm sprouts with garlic, green onions, sesame oil, seeds, salt and gochugaru.
Serve at room temperature or chilled.

recipes.title: Sigeumchi namul (seasoned spinach)
recipes.blurb: Quick-blanched spinach with sesame and garlic

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Blanch the spinach until just wilted.
Plunge into ice water, then squeeze out as much water as you can.
Loosen the spinach and toss with garlic, green onions, soy sauce and sesame oil.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve.

recipes.title: Oi muchim (spicy cucumber salad)
recipes.blurb: Crisp, tangy cucumber in gochugaru dressing

steps.text: Toss the cucumbers with the salt in a bowl.
Let sit, then squeeze out the liquid with your hands.
Mix gochugaru, vinegar, sugar, garlic and sesame oil.
Toss the cucumbers with the dressing and green onions.
Top with sesame seeds. Eat within a day.

recipes.title: Quick napa cabbage kimchi (geotjeori)
recipes.blurb: Fresh kimchi you can eat the same day

steps.text: Toss the cabbage with the salt in a large bowl. Let it sit, tossing every 15 minutes.
Salt the cabbage until bendy and wilted.
Rinse the cabbage well 2 or 3 times under cold water, then squeeze dry.
Mix gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, garlic and ginger into a paste.
Toss the cabbage with the paste and green onions, using gloves, until evenly coated.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds. Eat fresh, or pack into a jar and refrigerate up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Gyeran jjim (fluffy steamed egg)
recipes.blurb: Bubbling, souffle-like savory egg in a pot

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the salt until no streaks remain.
Whisk in the water and soy sauce, then pour through a sieve into a small heavy pot.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring gently with a spoon, until the egg starts to set.
Stop stirring, cover and cook on low until puffed and set.
Top with green onions, sesame oil and sesame seeds. Serve in the pot.

recipes.title: Gamja jorim (soy-braised potatoes)
recipes.blurb: Tender potatoes in a sweet soy glaze

steps.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a wide pan over medium heat and brown the potatoes lightly, 4 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, sugar, water and garlic. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until a knife slides in easily, stirring once or twice.
Uncover and boil down until the glaze is thick and shiny.
Stir in the syrup and sesame oil. Top with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Dubu jorim (spicy braised tofu)
recipes.blurb: Pan-seared tofu simmered in a savory-spicy sauce

steps.text: Pat the tofu very dry. Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown the tofu until golden on both sides, working in batches if needed.
Mix soy sauce, gochugaru, sugar, water, garlic and sesame oil.
Return the tofu to the pan in one layer. Spoon the sauce over it.
Simmer on low, basting, until the sauce is thick.
Top with green onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Myeolchi bokkeum (sweet-salty anchovies)
recipes.blurb: Crisp little anchovies in a sticky glaze, a classic lunchbox side

steps.text: Toast the anchovies in a dry nonstick skillet over medium heat until crisp, 3 minutes. Set aside.
Wipe out the pan. Add the oil, soy sauce, water, sugar and garlic.
Simmer the sauce until bubbly and a little thick.
Stir in the honey, then turn off the heat.
Add the anchovies and toss to coat. Mix in sesame oil and seeds.
Spread on parchment to cool so they do not stick.

recipes.title: Gaji namul (seasoned eggplant)
recipes.blurb: Silky steamed eggplant strips with soy-garlic dressing

steps.text: Set a steamer over boiling water.
Steam the eggplant until very tender.
Let it cool, then tear into thick strips and gently squeeze out extra liquid.
Mix soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, green onions, sugar and gochugaru.
Toss with the eggplant and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
